identity_assessments.name: CustomerSupport-AI-Agent
reasons: AI identity can perform high-impact Azure actions

findings.title: High-privilege Azure role: Owner
findings.message: CustomerSupport-AI-Agent is assigned Owner at subscription scope.
findings.remediation: Reduce the assignment to the narrowest built-in/custom role and smallest resource scope. Prefer managed identity for workloads and use PIM/JIT for human privilege.

findings.title: Wildcard Azure role permissions
findings.message: Role Owner grants wildcard control-plane or data-plane permissions.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcard permissions with explicit actions/dataActions required by the workload.

findings.title: Azure RBAC privilege-escalation capability
findings.message: Role Owner can create/change role assignments, role definitions, elevate access, or delegate managed identities.
findings.remediation: Remove Microsoft.Authorization write/elevate permissions from workload identities; isolate delegation roles and protect them with PIM and approval.

findings.title: Sensitive key/secret access in Azure role
findings.message: Role Owner includes access to secrets, keys, storage account keys, or AI service keys.
findings.remediation: Use least-privilege data-plane roles, managed identity, scoped Key Vault permissions, and disable local/key authentication on AI services where supported.

findings.title: Workload identity has broad Azure scope
findings.message: Machine identity CustomerSupport-AI-Agent has mutating/high-privilege access at subscription scope.
findings.remediation: Scope workload permissions to the specific resource group or resource required by the application/agent.

findings.title: AI identity has excessive Azure blast radius
findings.message: Likely AI/agent identity CustomerSupport-AI-Agent can materially change Azure resources or authorization.
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated managed identity for the AI workload, grant task-specific permissions only, add approval gates for high-impact actions, and continuously log agent activity.

findings.title: Azure AI account allows public network access
findings.message: AI/Cognitive Services account openai-prod explicitly allows public network access.
findings.remediation: For sensitive workloads, use private endpoints/network ACLs and explicitly disable public network access where architecture permits.

findings.title: Azure AI local/key authentication remains enabled
findings.message: AI/Cognitive Services account openai-prod reports disableLocalAuth=false.
findings.remediation: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID + managed identity and disable local/key authentication where supported by the workload.
